title: Recipe
description: A sophisticated and savory plant-based appetizer that mimics the classic French bistro dish using roasted beets and umami-rich sun-dried tomatoes. Perfect for impressing guests.
name: Vegan Steak Tartare

dry.name: Kala namak (black salt)
dry.notes: Gives an 'eggy' flavor to the yolk sauce

other.name: Shallot
other.notes: Small, peeled and very finely minced

instructions.description: Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Wash the beets, wrap each one in aluminum foil, and place on a baking sheet. Roast for 45-50 minutes, or until easily pierced with a fork. Allow to cool completely.

Once cooled, peel the beets (the skin should slip off easily) and dice them into very small, uniform 1/8-inch (3mm) cubes. This fine dice is crucial for the classic tartare texture. Place the diced beets in a medium bowl.

While the beets roast and cool, prepare the other components. In a small bowl, create the 'yolk' sauce by whisking together the vegan mayonnaise, nutritional yeast, kala namak, and a pinch of turmeric until smooth. Set aside.
To the bowl with the diced beets, add the finely chopped sun-dried tomatoes, minced shallot, capers, and cornichons.

Gently dress the mixture with the olive oil, Dijon mustard, vegan Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice, smoked paprika, and a few grinds of black pepper. Carefully stir to combine, being mindful not to mash the beets.
Gently fold in the chopped fresh parsley and chives. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.

To serve, use a ring mold to plate the tartare onto individual serving plates for a clean, professional look. Create a small well in the center of each portion and add a dollop of the 'yolk' sauce. Serve immediately with toasted baguette slices, crackers, or crispy french fries.

notes: For the best texture and flavor, do not use canned or pre-cooked beets. Roasting them fresh is key. The tartare can be made a few hours ahead and chilled, which allows the flavors to meld, but add the fresh herbs just before serving.
